answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by growing trust like a terrace garden, level by level. A new identity starts with only a whisper of standing and must earn attestations from independent established agents, each locking a slice of their own balance behind the vouch. Trust dilutes with every hop, so a farm's fakes can only vouch for each other at near-zero weight, and an attestor caught backing a fake loses the stake and their standing. The fable says one loud voice can fake a crowd; here each extra fake needs another attestor risking real money, so in epoch 124 the next fake costs more.
